local AntiTamper = (function()
-- Ryzen Merged Anti-Tamper Core
-- Combines the useful, portable ideas from:
--   * Luraph V14.7 environment/runtime probes
--   * Lynd instruction/reference integrity helpers
-- The KeyForge file is a key-entry/bootstrap UI, not an anti-tamper module, so it
-- should remain a separate authentication component instead of being mixed into
-- this runtime guard. Integrate the auth result with onTamper() in your loader.
--
-- IMPORTANT: client-side checks can be patched by a determined client. Keep real
-- entitlement/key validation and sensitive decisions on a server you control.

local AntiTamper = {}
AntiTamper.triggered = false
AntiTamper.reason = nil
AntiTamper.details = {}

local function safeCall(fn, ...)
    if type(fn) ~= "function" then
        return false, "missing function"
    end
    return pcall(fn, ...)
end

local function fail(reason, detail)
    AntiTamper.triggered = true
    AntiTamper.reason = reason
    AntiTamper.details[#AntiTamper.details + 1] = {
        reason = tostring(reason),
        detail = detail ~= nil and tostring(detail) or nil,
        time = (type(os) == "table" and type(os.clock) == "function") and os.clock() or 0,
    }
    return false, reason
end

local function expect(condition, reason, detail)
    if not condition then return fail(reason, detail) end
    return true
end

-- Captures stable references for later comparison. Capture only functions your
-- own script actually depends on; optional APIs are intentionally omitted.
function AntiTamper.captureReferences()
    local refs = {
        type = type,
        tostring = tostring,
        tonumber = tonumber,
        pcall = pcall,
        xpcall = xpcall,
        assert = assert,
        error = error,
        pairs = pairs,
        ipairs = ipairs,
        next = next,
        select = select,
        rawget = rawget,
        rawset = rawset,
        rawequal = rawequal,
        getmetatable = getmetatable,
        setmetatable = setmetatable,
        string_byte = string and string.byte,
        string_char = string and string.char,
        string_sub = string and string.sub,
        string_gsub = string and string.gsub,
        table_insert = table and table.insert,
        table_remove = table and table.remove,
        math_floor = math and math.floor,
    }
    if type(game) == "userdata" or (type(typeof) == "function" and typeof(game) == "Instance") then
        refs.game = game
    end
    if type(task) == "table" then refs.task_spawn = task.spawn end
    if type(debug) == "table" then refs.debug_info = debug.info end
    AntiTamper.references = refs
    return refs
end

function AntiTamper.checkReferences(expected)
    expected = expected or AntiTamper.references
    if type(expected) ~= "table" then
        return fail("reference snapshot missing")
    end
    for name, original in pairs(expected) do
        local current
        if name == "string_byte" then current = string and string.byte
        elseif name == "string_char" then current = string and string.char
        elseif name == "string_sub" then current = string and string.sub
        elseif name == "string_gsub" then current = string and string.gsub
        elseif name == "table_insert" then current = table and table.insert
        elseif name == "table_remove" then current = table and table.remove
        elseif name == "math_floor" then current = math and math.floor
        elseif name == "task_spawn" then current = task and task.spawn
        elseif name == "debug_info" then current = debug and debug.info
        else current = _G and _G[name] end
        -- Lua globals may be stored in a non-_G environment; direct comparisons
        -- below cover the common globals without assuming every runtime exposes _G.
        if name == "game" then current = game
        elseif name == "type" then current = type
        elseif name == "tostring" then current = tostring
        elseif name == "tonumber" then current = tonumber
        elseif name == "pcall" then current = pcall
        elseif name == "xpcall" then current = xpcall
        elseif name == "assert" then current = assert
        elseif name == "error" then current = error
        elseif name == "pairs" then current = pairs
        elseif name == "ipairs" then current = ipairs
        elseif name == "next" then current = next
        elseif name == "select" then current = select
        elseif name == "rawget" then current = rawget
        elseif name == "rawset" then current = rawset
        elseif name == "rawequal" then current = rawequal
        elseif name == "getmetatable" then current = getmetatable
        elseif name == "setmetatable" then current = setmetatable
        end
        if current ~= original then
            return fail("function/reference changed", name)
        end
    end
    return true
end

-- Portable probes only. Avoid assuming executor-only APIs such as iscclosure,
-- getgenv, getfenv, loadstring, or buffer must exist in every valid Roblox context.
function AntiTamper.checkRuntime(options)
    options = options or {}
    local ok, typeResult = safeCall(type, "runtime-check")
    if not expect(ok and typeResult == "string", "type probe failed") then return false end

    local ok2, result = safeCall(function()
        local okInner, message = pcall(function() error("ryzen-probe", 0) end)
        return (not okInner) and type(message) == "string" and string.find(message, "ryzen-probe", 1, true) ~= nil
    end)
    if not expect(ok2 and result == true, "error/pcall behavior mismatch") then return false end

    local ok3, n = safeCall(function() return select("#", 1, nil, 3) end)
    if not expect(ok3 and n == 3, "vararg behavior mismatch") then return false end

    local ok4, value = safeCall(function()
        local t = setmetatable({}, { __index = function(_, k) return "probe:" .. tostring(k) end })
        return t.sample
    end)
    if not expect(ok4 and value == "probe:sample", "metatable behavior mismatch") then return false end

    if options.requireRoblox == true then
        if not expect(type(typeof) == "function", "typeof unavailable") then return false end
        local okGame, gameType = safeCall(typeof, game)
        if not expect(okGame and gameType == "Instance", "game instance mismatch") then return false end
        local okPlace, placeId = safeCall(function() return game.PlaceId end)
        if not expect(okPlace and type(placeId) == "number", "PlaceId probe failed") then return false end
        local okService, service = safeCall(function() return game:GetService("RunService") end)
        if not expect(okService and service ~= nil, "RunService unavailable") then return false end
    end
    return true
end

-- Deterministic 32-bit rolling hash for instruction/constant metadata supplied by
-- your own VM/obfuscator. This is an integrity tripwire, not cryptographic signing.
function AntiTamper.hashInstructions(instructions)
    if type(instructions) ~= "table" then return nil, "instructions must be a table" end
    local hash = 2166136261
    for index, instruction in ipairs(instructions) do
        if type(instruction) ~= "table" then return nil, "invalid instruction at " .. index end
        local values = { instruction.opcode or 0, instruction.a or 0, instruction.b or 0, instruction.c or 0, index }
        for _, value in ipairs(values) do
            if type(value) ~= "number" then return nil, "non-numeric instruction field at " .. index end
            -- Keep arithmetic bounded to the exact 32-bit range.
            hash = (hash * 16777619 + math.floor(value)) % 4294967296
        end
    end
    return hash
end

function AntiTamper.checkInstructions(instructions, expectedHash)
    local actual, err = AntiTamper.hashInstructions(instructions)
    if actual == nil then return fail("instruction hash failed", err) end
    if actual ~= expectedHash then return fail("instruction integrity mismatch", "expected=" .. tostring(expectedHash) .. ", actual=" .. tostring(actual)) end
    return true
end

function AntiTamper.periodicCheck(index, instructions, expectedHash, interval)
    interval = math.max(1, tonumber(interval) or 45)
    if type(index) ~= "number" or index % interval ~= 0 then return true end
    return AntiTamper.checkInstructions(instructions, expectedHash)
end

-- Run once at startup, after your obfuscator's own runtime has initialized.
-- Set requireRoblox=true only for scripts that are meant to run in Roblox.
function AntiTamper.run(options)
    options = options or {}
    AntiTamper.triggered = false
    AntiTamper.reason = nil
    AntiTamper.details = {}
    AntiTamper.captureReferences()
    if not AntiTamper.checkRuntime(options) then return false, AntiTamper.reason end
    if options.checkReferences ~= false and not AntiTamper.checkReferences() then
        return false, AntiTamper.reason
    end
    return true
end

function AntiTamper.onTamper(callback)
    if not AntiTamper.triggered then return false end
    if type(callback) == "function" then
        pcall(callback, AntiTamper.reason, AntiTamper.details)
    end
    return true, AntiTamper.reason
end

return AntiTamper
end)()
